android.desc:
This keyboard is for people who frequently hit the wrong buttons on small displays and are frustrated by constantly deleting and retyping — without wanting to rely on autocorrection, which can also get things wrong.

The buttons are almost double the standard width, making it much easier to hit the right one. The tradeoff: each button shows two characters. To enter the character on the right, tap the button twice quickly (within 1/3 of a second; configurable). 

For each character, you briefly decide: once or twice?
You may type more slowly, but make fewer mistakes.
(If your device has a larger screen, you probably don't need this app.)

To access settings, long-press the globe icon and select the gear icon in the popup. You can adjust the double-tap timing, enable a dedicated number row, show special character hints for faster symbol entry, and more.

quotes.text:
This is a keyboard app for people who frequently hit the wrong buttons on small displays and are frustrated by constantly deleting and retyping — without wanting to rely on autocorrection.

The buttons are almost double the standard width, making it much easier to hit the right one. The tradeoff: each button shows two characters. To enter the character on the right, tap the button twice quickly.

For each character, you briefly decide: once or twice? You may type more slowly, but make fewer mistakes.

(There's an alternative long-tap mode that can be enabled in prefs, with that you have to tap slightly longer to get the second character, instead of double tapping.)

Background story: I have had the idea for this app for over a year. I had already identified that the existing Simple Keyboard app (from Raimondas Rimkus) would be a good starting point. With AI assistance I built the initial version of this Widekey Keyboard app in a single day.

Github: https://github.com/kaie/widekey-keyboard

Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=de.kuix.widekeykeyboard

I hope the app can be helpful for some people!
